commits.message:
effects-feel: the whole element rests between breaths, and neighbours hold at any swing (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Review high (escalation) on #322:
- REACH 0.5 -> 0.12: a sigh is done 0.86 into its turn at the heart, so
  with half a turn of lag the edges were still exhaling when the next
  breath began, and the element never rested. Now every turn has a
  moment where nothing is lit, at 40, 104 and 1024 columns.
- SPREAD 0.005 -> 0.003 and the fill term gentler along the row (noise
  at 0.025 a column, smoothstep over -0.5..0.5): neighbours under 0.02
  at swing 1 under every continuous ease, not only the defaults. Step
  eases jump by design; the docstring now says "continuous".
- The 0.06 offset had no job once drift is measured from t=0; gone.
  drift(0) is computed once. The per-cell `depth` is `fill`, so it no
  longer shares a word with a breath's strength.
- Tests sample real columns at three z; the app test watches two breaths
  rather than one instant a cell may be resting at.

effects-feel: a breath spreads a column at a time on a narrow element (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Review medium on #322: lag as a share of span stepped neighbours past a
just-noticeable difference on badges of 12 columns or fewer (0.046 at 6).
The rate per column is now min(SPREAD, REACH / span): bounded per column
for neighbours, bounded across the width for forward phase. Test: adjacent
cells under 0.02 at 6, 12, 40 and 1024 columns (red at 6 and 12 before).

effects-feel: a breath reaches the edges in one share of its turn at any width (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Review high on #322: SPREAD per column let the heart's wander drag phase
backward on wide elements, the 0.1 drift could start a cell off rest at
t=0 for some z, and 40% depth meant no sigh reached its swing.

- lag is REACH (0.5 turn) times distance over span, so the forward-phase
  bound no longer depends on width
- drift is measured from t=0, so every cell starts at rest at any z
- depth goes through a smoothstep: deep stretches fill to the whole swing
- tests sweep z, check the field is exactly 0 at t=0 (red before at
  z=82.14), and that every cell swells once and ebbs once per breath at
  40, 104 and 1024 columns

effects-feel: a breath blooms from its heart and fills the row unevenly (rich-effects-fxiy.b6i)

Spread 0.0012 -> 0.005 of a breath per column, so warmth visibly rolls out
from the wandering heart; depth varies 40% along the row, not 15%; breath
lengths drift 0.1 of a turn, not 0.03. Worst 1 fps step 0.0368 over 3600 s
x 4 z x 2 offsets x spans {40,104} (bar 0.04).
test(highlighter): compare Rich's code-point span offsets as UTF-16, pin a token after an astral character (rich-highlighter-xwqv)
test(highlighter): pin U+2029 and an astral word character against Rich; scope the Python-class comment (rich-highlighter-xwqv)

fix(highlighter): JSONHighlighter reads \w, \b, \d and . as Rich's Python does (rich-highlighter-xwqv)

Rich compiles its JSON patterns on a str, where \w, \b and \d are Unicode
and . stops only at \n. JSONHighlighter used JavaScript's ASCII classes,
so `étrue` gained a bool and `é"x"` a string Rich never lays. It now
uses the Python-class consts ReprHighlighter already spells, under `u`.

test/core/json-highlight.test.ts pins spans and printed bytes against a
golden generated from Rich 15.0.0 alone, and absorbs the four
hand-copied Rich expectations that sat in highlighter.test.ts.

fix(highlighter)!: ISO8601Highlighter lays Rich's spans in Rich's colours (rich-highlighter-6cj4) (#321)

* fix(highlighter)!: ISO8601Highlighter lays Rich's spans in Rich's colours (rich-highlighter-6cj4)

ISO8601Highlighter now carries Rich 15.0.0's patterns: each matches a whole
string that is one ISO 8601 value and lays year/month/day/week/hour/minute/
second/frac/ms/hyphen spans under date/time/timezone. iso8601.date is blue,
iso8601.time magenta, iso8601.timezone yellow, as in rich.default_styles.

BREAKING CHANGE: a date or time inside other text ("date: 2023-01-15") is no
longer highlighted; Rich's patterns are anchored to the whole string.

test/core/iso8601-highlight.golden.json is Rich's own output for its
iso8601_highlight_tests corpus plus three edge cases.

* fix(highlighter): the default theme names every part ISO8601Highlighter lays (rich-highlighter-6cj4)

The year, month, day, week, hour, minute, second, frac, ms and hyphen
groups reached onStyleError as unknown names, so a strict handler threw on
every timestamp. They are NULL_STYLE, as Rich draws them, and a test now
requires every built-in's group names in DEFAULT_STYLES.

Also: one TZ and COMPACT_TIME fragment each, the docs row names the
date-time forms and the per-part keys, and styledTimestamp's comment says
what it draws for a short string.
